title: Anomalous Mobility Enhancement in Restricted Geometries
abstract: We investigate the effect of geometrical confinement on driven transport in anomalous media within the framework of the quenched trap model. The particle performs a biased random walk on a lattice, where quenched disorder introduces power-law distributed trapping times. We consider channels that are infinite along one direction and have a finite cross-section in the remaining $d-1$ directions. In the glassy regime, where $α=T/T_g<1$, we derive an analytical expression for the mean longitudinal displacement in the long-time and weak-force limits. We find the scaling $\langle x_\parallel(t)\rangle \propto F_\parallel^αt^αΩ^{-(1-α)}$, where $F_\parallel>0$ is the effective longitudinal force and $Ω$ is the number of sites in a transverse cross-section. Thus, the anomalous mobility is enhanced for narrower channels. Our analytical result applies to general Bravais lattices in $d$ dimensions with periodic transverse boundary conditions. Numerical simulations confirm the analytical predictions for different lattice geometries and show quantitative agreement even for channels with reflecting boundary conditions.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes driven transport in disordered media confined to narrow channels using the Quenched Trap Model. It derives an analytical scaling law demonstrating that anomalous mobility is paradoxically enhanced as the channel cross-section shrinks. The work is significant for understanding how geometric constraints modify non-equilibrium dynamics in disordered quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how geometrical confinement affects anomalous transport in disordered media, specifically challenging the intuition that increased confinement always slows down particle motion.
main_result: The analysis derives a scaling law showing that anomalous mobility is enhanced (increases) as the transverse cross-section of the channel decreases, contrary to simple expectations.
method: The authors use analytical derivations involving the quenched trap model (QTM) and employ double subordination techniques in the Laplace domain to calculate the disorder-averaged propagator and mean displacement.
model_or_system: The system is a particle undergoing a biased random walk on a lattice subject to quenched disorder, modeled by power-law distributed trapping times. The geometry is restricted to channels infinite in one direction but finite in the others.
key_observables: Mean longitudinal displacement $\langle x_{\parallel}(t) angle$, anomalous mobility ($\mu$), and the return probability ($Q_0$).
important_parameters: The glassy regime parameter $\alpha = T/T_g < 1$, the effective longitudinal force $F_\parallel$, and the transverse cross-section size $\Omega$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the motion occurs on a $d$-dimensional Bravais lattice and initially relies on periodic transverse boundary conditions, though results are shown to be robust for reflecting boundaries.
figures_summary: Figure 5 compares simulated mean longitudinal displacement vs. transverse width for reflecting boundaries against analytical predictions derived for periodic boundary conditions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing the QTM, calculating the return probability, deriving the mobility dependence on disorder parameters, and concluding with a discussion of the results and generalizations to various lattice geometries.
why_interesting: The study of anomalous transport and aging in disordered media is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in complex quantum systems, such as those modeled by spin glasses or disordered quantum magnets.
